answers.title: Short Answer
answers.markdown:
Java is a **high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language** designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible.

It follows the idea of **Write Once, Run Anywhere** through the JVM.

answers.title: Interview Answer
answers.markdown:
Java source code is compiled into **bytecode**. The bytecode runs on the **Java Virtual Machine (JVM)**, which provides platform independence.

### Key characteristics
- Object-oriented
- Platform independent
- Garbage collected
- Strongly typed
- Large standard library

question: What is the difference between HashMap and ConcurrentHashMap?

answers.title: Comparison
answers.markdown:
| Feature | HashMap | ConcurrentHashMap |
|---|---|---|
| Thread safe | No | Yes |
| Null keys | One | Not allowed |
| Null values | Allowed | Not allowed |
| Concurrent access | Not designed for it | Designed for it |

Use `ConcurrentHashMap` when multiple threads need to update/read the map concurrently.
